newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes end down as sellers sidelined.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes end down as sellers sidelined.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude values ended lower in subdued Tuesday discussions, as key sellers of Alaskan oil waited to see if problems at the Valdez port would delay loadings of oil tankers.
Two ships operated by BP America and one by Arco waited at Valdez Tuesday as a probe continued into an oil slick spotted in the port late last week.
Officials said the slick was not caused by the ships but investigators said it was likely a ballast-water-treatment plant.
The plant remained closed for an unspecified duration, according to state and federal officials.
This prevented tankers from leaving with full loads of oil, traders said.
Meanwhile, ANS prices continued to follow NYMEX, falling to $23.47/23.67. The discount held at $1.53 under February West Texas Intermediate (WTI) following two deals January 8.
A deal for Kern River heavy crude was done Monday at 15 cents under postings, traders said.
A second heavy deal was done early this week. A trader said they bought at a level tighter than 15 cents under and that volume was between 2,000 and 4,000 barrels per day.
